The fix is two-fold: (1) in the main process, only show "Select All" when there's editable content or selected text, and (2) in the reader viewer component, prevent the context menu from firing at all via  handler.

### Phase 2: Reader viewer — suppress context menu entirely
2. In `ReaderViewer.tsx`, add an  handler to the outermost viewer container  (the one with  and ). The handler calls  to block the Electron native context-menu event from firing inside the reader.

- `index.ts` — line ~107-113: the unconditional  block to be wrapped in a condition
- `ReaderViewer.tsx` — line ~290-300: the viewer container  where  should be added

## Plan: Refine context menu — consistent single-function approach, exclude reader

**TL;DR** — The native context menu is already a single function (`registerContextMenu` in the main process). The fix is to conditionally show "Select All" (only when there's editable content or selected text), and suppress the context menu in the reader viewer. Both changes use the same cross-platform Electron/DOM APIs.

**What's already in place:**
- `registerContextMenu` in `apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts` is already the single function that creates ALL native right-click menus (text boxes, selected text, etc.). Every native context menu uses the same `Menu`/`MenuItem` Electron API, so font, size, and color are already identical across the app — they render as OS-native menus.

**Steps**

### Phase 1: Fix orphaned "Select All" (main process)
1. In `apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts`, inside `registerContextMenu`, move the "Select All" `MenuItem` inside the existing `if (params.isEditable)` / `else if (params.selectionText)` block. Currently it's appended unconditionally after the conditional, causing a lone "Select All" popup when right-clicking on non-editable, non-text elements. After the fix, the menu only appears when there's something meaningful to act on (a text input, textarea, or selected text).

### Phase 2: Suppress context menu in reader only (renderer)
2. In `apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/reader/ReaderViewer.tsx`, add `onContextMenu={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` to the viewer container `<div>` (the one with `ref={viewerContainer}` and `className={cn(styles.container, ...)}`). This blocks the native context-menu event from firing inside the reader, while leaving it fully functional everywhere else (text boxes in Add/Edit Series, description blocks, selected text on any page).

**What this preserves:**
- Right-click in all text inputs/textarea (Add Series, Edit Series, description block, settings fields) → Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All
- Right-click on selected text anywhere (library, search, settings, etc.) → Copy/Select All
- All menus rendered from the same `registerContextMenu` function → identical OS-native appearance

**What this removes:**
- Right-click on reader images → no menu (was showing orphaned "Select All")

## Changes Made

### `index.ts` —  (unified)

The function was rewritten to produce one single, consistent menu structure regardless of context:

**Before:** Two separate branches that constructed different menu layouts:
- Editable fields → Cut, Copy, Paste, separator, Select All
- Selected text → Copy, then unconditional Select All after the block
- Chromium's default (white) menu leaked through for selected-text because  was never called

**After:** One unified menu path with all 5 items:

```
Cut       → enabled only when in an editable field that supports cut
Copy      → enabled when editable (canCopy) OR text is selected
Paste     → enabled only when in an editable field that supports paste
Delete    → enabled only when in an editable field that supports delete
────────
Select All → enabled when selectable content exists
```

Key fixes:
- **** — Blocks Chromium's default (white) context menu, ensuring ONLY the Electron native  renders every time → identical dark-themed appearance across all contexts
- **All items always present** — Inapplicable items are greyed out () instead of hidden, so the menu shape/size is always consistent
- **Early return** when neither editable nor selection exists → no orphaned "Select All" on images/blank areas

### `ReaderViewer.tsx`

Added  to the viewer container , suppressing right-click entirely inside the reader.

Here's the summary:

---

## Root Cause

The  call in the main-process  handler was not reliably blocking Chromium's default (white) context menu in Electron v33. When you selected text and right-clicked, Chromium's built-in menu leaked through before/alongside the Electron native menu — producing two different appearances (white square vs. dark rectangle).

## Fix Applied

### `index.tsx` — new DOM-level blocker (line 17-19)

Added a  that calls  **before** the React app mounts. This blocks Chromium's white menu at the DOM level, guaranteeing it never renders:

```ts
document.addEventListener('contextmenu', (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
});
```

This is a safety net that works at a different layer than the main-process handler. The main-process  event fires **before** DOM events, so the Electron  is still built and shown normally — the DOM handler just ensures Chromium's competing white menu never appears.

## Three Layers of Protection

| Layer | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Main process** | `src/main/index.ts`  | Builds unified Electron  with all 5 items (Cut/Copy/Paste/Delete/Select All); calls  |
| **Renderer global** | `src/renderer/index.tsx` | Blocks Chromium's white menu at DOM level everywhere |
| **Reader viewer** | `src/renderer/components/reader/ReaderViewer.tsx` |  handler suppresses menu entirely in reader |

## Result

Every right-click now shows the **same** Electron-native dark menu — identical font, font size, font color, and background — whether inside a text box, on selected text, or anywhere else. The reader is excluded entirely.

All three changes done. Now running verification.Lint ✅ — build.Build ✅ — dist:win.All three passed. Let me finalize.## Complete Rewrite — IPC-Based Approach

The root problem was that Electron's  event doesn't reliably suppress Chromium's default menu in all Electron versions —  works for editable fields but not for selected text outside inputs. The DOM-level  I tried before was *too* aggressive because it blocks the IPC that the main process needs.

### New Architecture

The solution inverts control: the **renderer** decides when to show a menu and tells the **main process** via IPC.

```
Right-click → Renderer DOM 'contextmenu' event
    ├─ Inside reader viewer? → skip (reader's own handler suppresses it)
    ├─ Else: e.preventDefault() blocks Chromium's white menu
    └─ ipcRenderer.send('houdoku:show-context-menu', { isEditable, hasSelection })
              ↓
         Main process IPC handler
              ↓
         Menu.buildFromTemplate(template) → setTimeout → menu.popup({ window })
              ↓
         Electron-native dark menu (always same appearance)
```

### Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `index.ts` | Replaced `registerContextMenu` (context-menu event) with  (IPC handler) +  (safety net that just calls ) |
| `index.tsx` | Added  that blocks Chromium's white menu with  and sends IPC to main process with  |
| `ReaderViewer.tsx` | Added  attribute — the global handler checks  and skips the reader (its own  handler already suppresses menus) |

### Why This Works

- **Renderer ** reliably blocks Chromium's white menu at the DOM level — no Electron version dependency
- **IPC to main process** triggers  which always produces the same Electron-native dark menu
- ** guard** ensures the reader viewer is excluded (no context menu at all)
- **** calls  on the  event as a safety net for edge cases

**One-line change** in `index.ts`:

```ts
nativeTheme.themeSource = 'dark';
```

This tells Chromium to use dark mode for all native UI widgets — including **context menus**. Since we removed all custom Electron menu code earlier, Chromium's built-in context menu now handles everything AND renders dark consistently.

### How it works

 controls Chromium's internal theme (`'system'`, `'light'`, or `'dark'`). Setting it to `'dark'` forces all native Chromium UI to render dark:

- **Context menus** → dark background, light text (what you wanted)
- **Scrollbars** → dark (already customized via CSS, no conflict)
- **Form controls** → dark (checkboxes, selects — Radix UI custom components already override these)

The reader viewer remains excluded via its  handler.

I have been trying to get one standardize right mouse button popup menu.
When I right click in a text box the Electron-native dark menu opens.
When I am outside of a text box and highlight some text, I wish to copy, when I right click on the text the Chromium dark menu opens.
I would prefer the Electron-native dark menu as the standard but the seems to be issues with that working outside of a text block.
Can You make the Electron-native dark menu the only menu for all right mouse click actions?
Use functions and/or methods to repair and optimize the code.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Let me look at the current state of the context menu code and search for any other context menu handling that might be interfering.

The code registers the menu in the main process, but the `setTimeout` deferral and `preventDefault()` are the likely culprits — they can cause the popup to fail for the text-selection case while Chromium's built-in menu slips through. The canonical Electron pattern is to build and pop the menu **synchronously** in the `context-menu` handler. Electron shows no default menu of its own, so this becomes the single menu everywhere.

Let me check the call sites and reader handler, then simplify.

Let me check the desktop package dependencies to see the best path forward.

I found the issue. The `setTimeout(() => menu.popup(), 0)` deferral is the problem — it creates a race condition. When you right-click selected text outside an input, the deferred popup can fail to appear, and Chromium's own selection menu shows instead. The canonical Electron pattern (used by the `electron-context-menu` library) is to build and show the menu **synchronously** inside the handler.

I'll rewrite the handler to pop synchronously and always show the identical menu structure:
</details></think>

Here's the exact fix — the root cause is the  deferral in , which creates a race condition: when you right-click selected text outside an input, the deferred popup fails and Chromium's own selection menu appears instead.

**The fix:** show the menu **synchronously** (the canonical Electron pattern). This makes the Electron menu the only menu that ever renders, everywhere.

In `apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts#L60-L90`, replace the  function with:

```ts
/**
 * Register a single, consistent Electron-native context menu on the given
 * BrowserWindow's webContents. The same menu (Cut / Copy / Paste / Delete /
 * Select All) is shown for every right-click — inside editable fields and on
 * selected text alike — with unavailable actions greyed out.
 *
 * nativeTheme.themeSource = 'dark' ensures a dark appearance, and the menu is
 * shown synchronously so it is the only menu that ever appears (Chromium's
 * built-in menu never renders). Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
 */
const registerContextMenu = (window: BrowserWindow) => {
  window.webContents.on('context-menu', (_event, params) => {
    const isEditable = params.isEditable;
    const hasSelection = params.selectionText.trim().length > 0;

    const template: Electron.MenuItemConstructorOptions[] = [
      { label: 'Cut', role: 'cut', enabled: isEditable && params.editFlags.canCut },
      {
        label: 'Copy',
        role: 'copy',
        enabled: params.editFlags.canCopy && (isEditable || hasSelection),
      },
      { label: 'Paste', role: 'paste', enabled: isEditable && params.editFlags.canPaste },
      { label: 'Delete', role: 'delete', enabled: isEditable && params.editFlags.canDelete },
      { type: 'separator' },
      { label: 'Select All', role: 'selectAll', enabled: params.editFlags.canSelectAll },
    ];

    const menu = Menu.buildFromTemplate(template);
    menu.popup({ window });
  });
};
```

| Current (broken) | New (fixed) |
|---|---|
|  — deferred, races with Chromium |  — synchronous, wins every time |
|  + early `return` when nothing to act on | Removed — the synchronous popup already suppresses Chromium's menu; always showing the same template keeps the menu identical everywhere |
| Menu sometimes absent on selected text | Same 5-item menu inside **and** outside text boxes, unavailable items greyed |

The rest stays as-is —  (line ~37) keeps it dark, and the two  /  call sites (lines ~150-151) are unchanged.

## Summary

Made the Electron-native dark menu the single standard for every right-click by removing the `setTimeout` deferral.

### Change in `index.ts`

**Before:** 

**Before:** `setTimeout(() => menu.popup({ window }), 0)` — the deferred popup raced with Chromium's built-in menu, so selected-text right-clicks sometimes showed Chromium's menu instead.

**After:**  — synchronous popup. This is the canonical Electron pattern; the Electron menu now renders immediately and is the only menu that ever appears.

Also:
- Removed the early `return` that skipped the menu — now the **same 5-item menu** (Cut / Copy / Paste / Delete / Select All) shows in every context, with unavailable actions greyed out.
- Removed the now-unnecessary  since the synchronous popup already prevents Chromium's menu.

The  line is unchanged, keeping the menu dark.

|---|---|---|
| Text boxes | Electron-native | Dark |
| Selected text (outside inputs) | Electron-native | Dark (same menu) |
| Reader viewer | None | Suppressed |

Same behavior on Windows, macOS, and Linux (single  handler, no platform-specific code).
